I want to see him. I have no right to demand it.
Nora places a sealed envelope between herself and Elena. Her hands shake but her voice does not.
If I give this to you, you promise my current address never enters a family file.
Independent counsel holds the originals. Your decision to testify can change at any time.
I don’t need Luca’s address. Tell him there is a door he can open if he wants.
Nora studies him. At last she unfolds a photograph of Luca beside a repaired blue fishing boat.
Nora enters Elena's office through the front door. She insisted on being seen arriving on her own terms.
I didn't disappear because I wanted a mystery. I disappeared because someone used my signature on accounts I never opened.
You can stop the interview at any moment. No one here gets to promise you immunity they cannot grant.
Nora looks at Dante. "Your brother tried to warn me. He was frightened of you finding out because he thought you would come in with guns."
Dante swallows. "He wasn't entirely wrong about who I used to be."
The room stays quiet long enough for Nora to finish her sentence herself.

beats.hint: How do you support Nora’s testimony?

opts.t: Let Elena lead; document every claim.
then: Nora agrees to an attorney-led statement with defined redactions.

opts.t: Ask what protection Nora wants, not what Dante can give.
then: Nora asks for relocation funds managed by an independent nonprofit.

opts.t: Step outside so Nora can speak without the Morettis present.
then: Dante follows your lead; Nora is able to speak more freely to Elena.

beats.place: A witness with her own voice

beats: Nora meets Elena in a room where the windows look onto a public street. She refuses the private room Vince first booked.
I have spent six years listening to powerful men explain why I should be hidden. I want a table near the door.
Elena lets her choose the recorder, the legal observer, and the questions she won't answer today. Dante waits downstairs and does not ask for her address.
Luca didn't steal. He copied records because he thought ordinary people deserved to know who owned the shore.
There is more to her story than the case: she once wanted to become a teacher. You ask whether she still does.
Maybe when this is over. I forgot people were allowed to ask me that.

choices.t: Support a letter that Luca can choose to answer.
then: Dante writes three drafts before settling on six honest lines.

choices.t: Focus on safeguarding Nora’s testimony.
then: Nora chooses independent counsel and retains control of her statement.

choices.t: Ask Dante what he would do if Luca refuses.
then: 'Then I love him from a distance. I think I finally understand how.'

en.title: The Last Bargain

goal.zh: Expose antagonist through civic mechanisms, no vigilante resolution.
goal.en: Expose antagonist through civic mechanisms, no vigilante resolution.

then: Nora reads her carefully redacted statement once more. Elena does not rush her into signing.
The relocation fund is managed outside the Moretti companies, exactly as Nora asked.
Nora speaks more freely without Dante in the room. Her testimony has details the family never knew.

beats: The city announces an emergency public hearing on the redevelopment project. Salvatore arrives with lawyers and a threat to bury the foundation in litigation.
Dante can keep the waterfront and the woman if he signs the settlement.
You are still talking as though people are property.
The settlement waives the residents’ right to review the land transfer.
Behind you sit families whose homes would be demolished under the plan.

then: Luca has not answered the letter yet. It belongs to him to decide when—or whether—he writes back.
Nora has a new lawyer and a safe way to testify. Neither of us needs to know where she is.
If my brother never comes home, I will still try to make this city safer. He owes me nothing.

beats: We reject the settlement. We disclose the records and let the public review the project.
He slides the microphone to you, but does not switch it on. You can speak or remain silent.
The remaining evidence places Salvatore’s shell companies at every diversion. It is enough to seek an injunction.
You notice Dante waiting—not for your approval, but for your own choice.
The settlement offers new homes to only a third of the displaced families. The others are missing from the list.
A resident named Mrs. Alvarez stands in the hallway holding a lease written decades ago.
I used to call this neighborhood an asset. Mrs. Alvarez calls it home. She has the better word.
You will throw away an empire for a handful of tenants?
No. I am refusing to let an empire throw them away.

then: Dante brings Luca’s unopened letter but does not hand it to you without asking. It belongs to Luca, not to the family empire.
He should be able to decide when his story is told.
Elena confirms Nora’s address was never included in the shared case packet, preserving her right to testify safely.
Protection means she still gets to choose what to say.
The family lawyer asks whether Luca will testify. You remind him that missing does not mean obligated.
She is right. Find another way to prove the case.

beats: The evidence is not dramatic: three signatures on a bank transfer, one altered board minute, and a paper trail that refuses to vanish.
Salvatore authorized the shell company. The original approval was scanned before the modification.
The building's access records show who entered after hours. They do not prove intent, but they support Nora's timeline.
Then we bring it to the authorities and let the evidence speak. No private retaliation.
You receive a brief message through Elena's protected contact line: LUCA IS SAFE. HE IS NOT READY TO MEET.
Dante reads it once. "I wish he were. But ready is not mine to decide."

beats.hint: What is your next ethical step?

opts.t: Preserve the original evidence with the prosecutor.
then: Elena obtains a receipt chain so every transfer can be audited.
The press release omits Nora’s identity, at her request.

opts.t: Tell Dante not to pressure Luca into coming home.
then: He sends one reply: "I hear you. I will be here if you want me."

beats.place: The page no one can sign away

beats: Before the hearing, Mrs. Alvarez produces a box of old rent receipts. Salvatore's attorney calls them irrelevant.
They're evidence people lived here before anyone decided the land was an investment opportunity.
Dante reads one receipt dated the year he was born. He had been telling himself the waterfront belonged to his family since childhood; the paper says otherwise.
A reporter asks whether he is sacrificing his fortune for a woman. Dante replies without looking at you for approval.
No. I'm correcting harm that should never have happened. She helped me see it. That doesn't make the harm about us.
When the hearing resumes, you choose your seat. It is not beside Dante unless you want it to be.

choices.t: Speak for the affected residents, with their permission.
then: Your statement centers their housing rights, not Dante’s image.

choices.t: Submit the evidence through Elena.
then: The hearing enters the ledger into the public record.

choices.t: Refuse to become his public symbol.
then: Dante nods. 'You don’t owe my redemption a face.'

en.title: The Cost of a Crown

goal.zh: Crown is abdicated, commitment follows character not power.
goal.en: Crown is abdicated, commitment follows character not power.

then: Evidence receipts accompany the transfer to prosecutors. Every item can now be checked for tampering.
Nora’s name is omitted from the public announcement at her explicit request.
Dante sends Luca one message without demanding a reply. He keeps his promise afterward.

beats: Salvatore’s injunction hearing fails. The board votes to suspend him pending investigation, but several investors demand Dante cut ties with the foundation to protect profits.
If you give up the waterfront, you could lose the chairmanship.
Then I lose it. The city doesn’t belong to my family.
He signs control of the emergency scholarship fund over to an independent board.
I spent years mistaking the chair for the person sitting in it.

then: The residents asked you to speak again. They remember you listened before you took the microphone.
Elena filed the evidence in your name, with your approval. The hearing is no longer my family’s private argument.
The posters will not use your face. You refused to become my good-news story, and I made sure they listened.

beats: In the empty boardroom, Dante takes off his watch and sets it beside the unsigned resignation letter.
I won’t ask you to stay because I’m changing. Change is what I owe the people I hurt.
But I will ask one honest thing: if there were no name, no money, no danger—would you still want to know me?
The office feels different without the men waiting outside. It feels like a room where two adults can choose.
After the vote, reporters gather below. Dante chooses the service elevator and the coffee machine that takes three attempts to work.
I gave up the chairmanship this morning. The world did not end. Apparently the coffee did.
He offers you a paper cup with a crooked handwritten label: YOURS, IF YOU WANT IT.
I want to build a business whose books can be read in daylight. That will take years.
He looks tired, not heroic. For the first time you can imagine knowing him on an ordinary Tuesday.

beats.place: The price of signing away a crown

beats: The independent auditor arrives with a list of companies that must be sold or placed under separate supervision.
You can keep your personal fortune. You cannot keep undisclosed control over the land trust and call it independent.
Then take the controls away. Publish the timetable.
Salvatore's lawyer offers a last private exit: an agreement that protects the family name if Dante withdraws his complaint.
Dante pushes it back across the table without opening it.
I do not get to keep my reputation by spending someone else's future.
He looks at you, but he does not ask you to applaud.

then: The auditor drafts a public reporting schedule independent of Dante’s consent.
The council elects its own negotiators, and the settlement remains reviewable.

opts.t: Ask Dante what he plans to do without the empire.
then: He answers after a long silence: "Find work that does not make anyone afraid to say no."

beats: June calls from the scholarship office. The fund has been transferred to independent trustees, but the first payment is still delayed by a week.
You both keep saying things are better. I still have a tuition deadline.
Dante doesn't ask her to be patient. He calls Elena and the bank's compliance team to arrange an emergency bridge through the residents' nonprofit, with published terms.
Resigning is a statement. Paying the students is the work.
He goes back to the empty office and starts packing books. He asks whether you want to help; when you say you have your own work, he says he understands.
The future takes shape not as a dramatic sacrifice, but as the tedious obligation to keep your promises.

choices.t: Tell him the man matters more than the title.
then: 'Then I will work on becoming someone worth knowing.'

choices.t: Ask what daily life with him would actually be like.
then: You discuss time, work, safety, privacy, and who gets to say no.

choices.t: Say you cannot decide yet.
then: 'That’s fair. There is no deadline on your heart.'

en.title: The Life He Cannot Buy

goal.zh: Show sustainable affection in everyday life.
goal.en: Show sustainable affection in everyday life.

then: The independent auditor posts the first oversight timetable; it will continue even if Dante leaves office.
The elected resident negotiators publish a settlement summary in language their neighbors can understand.
Dante begins looking for work where his name carries less weight than his competence.

beats: After the board vote, Dante asks if he can see your ordinary Saturday. No private restaurant, no stylist, no driver. Just the life you already have.
He burns toast in your kitchen, refuses to blame the toaster, and asks how you like your coffee.
You are allowed to laugh. I’ve threatened men for less, but the toast won fair and square.
The doorbell rings. A courier brings a small envelope addressed in familiar handwriting: LUCA.
Would you mind if I read it here? I don’t want to disappear on you.

then: I have spent my life defending a name. You looked at the man underneath it. I do not want to waste that.
I asked Mara how to cook without an assistant. She gave me a list and laughed in my face.
I will not hand you a deadline for deciding how you feel. I can wait without putting my life on hold.

beats: The letter says only: I AM SAFE. I NEED TIME. I SAW WHAT YOU DID FOR THE WATERFRONT.
Dante closes his eyes. He does not ask you to explain what the letter means.
He doesn’t have to come back. It’s enough to know he can choose.
He reaches for your hand halfway, then lets it hover. Your answer still matters even in a tender moment.
At the corner market, Dante has no idea how much tomatoes cost. The cashier recognizes you and speaks to you first.
I have been overpaying for vegetables my entire life. Does this count as a scandal?
A neighbor asks whether he is helping you move. Dante waits for you to introduce him however you like.
I can carry the bags. I can also learn to be quiet when you want an afternoon that belongs only to you.
Back home, the letter from Luca arrives without a return address. The privacy feels like a gift.
The supermarket is bright, crowded, and entirely uninterested in Dante Moretti. A woman asks him to move his cart out of the aisle.
You laugh. He looks pleased, even as he studies the bewildering selection of pasta.
I know how to acquire a restaurant chain. I have absolutely no idea which tomatoes you use for sauce.
At checkout, the cashier recognizes you from the waterfront meeting and thanks you for helping get the records published.
My aunt kept her apartment. That's what mattered.
Dante does not interrupt the exchange. For once, he is content to be the person holding the shopping bags.

beats.hint: What ordinary moment do you choose?

opts.t: Cook dinner at your place, if you invite him.
then: He asks what to bring and arrives at the time you choose.

opts.t: Go to the neighborhood bookshop alone.
then: He wishes you a good afternoon and makes no surprise appearance.

opts.t: Invite Mara and Elena to a casual meal.
then: The evening becomes a conversation about recipes and school funding, not romance.

beats: At the market Dante picks up the wrong herbs twice, then asks a teenager restocking shelves how to tell them apart. He listens carefully to the answer.
My entire financial education did not prepare me for cilantro.
You have an appointment later in the afternoon. He asks when you would like to part ways, rather than constructing an excuse to linger.
A resident from the harbor committee stops to thank you for insisting on the public meeting. Dante steps aside so you can have the conversation without him.
Walking back, he says quietly: "I like the way people know you without knowing me. I think that's how it should be."
You carry your own bag if you wish. He stops asking whether you need saving, and begins asking what you actually need.

choices.t: Take his hand and plan a simple date.
then: He suggests walking to the market and learning which fruit you like.

choices.t: Talk about separate careers and space.
then: You agree neither person will be absorbed into the other’s world.

choices.t: Spend the afternoon as friends.
then: Dante accepts the label without trying to bargain it into something else.

en.title: The Question He Finally Asks

goal.zh: Meaningful non-punitive relationship commitment choice.
goal.en: Meaningful non-punitive relationship commitment choice.

then: The dinner you invited him to has no staff and no cameras. Dante shows up on time with groceries.
You went to the bookshop alone. Nobody appears uninvited, and Dante never asks for a report of your afternoon.
Mara and Elena keep discussing the scholarship budget long after the plates are cleared.

beats: The hearings have ended for now. The foundation is independently run. Luca is safe. Dante invites you to the same rooftop where you first saw the city from his side of the glass.
When we met, I thought power meant never hearing no. You showed me it means having the strength to hear it.
No expensive box sits between you. No cameras. Just a bench, the skyline, and two cups of takeaway coffee.
I love you. You don’t have to say it back. I wanted you to know without a deal attached.

then: Mara has the table ready. No security performance, no cameras. Just dinner and whatever you want to talk about.
Your work has its own funding and office now. I like knowing we can choose each other without merging our lives.
That afternoon as friends mattered. I am not going to erase it by asking a different question tonight.

beats: He takes a breath, and asks the question he has avoided turning into a demand.
What kind of future would you actually want—with me, without me, or somewhere in between?
You can hear a train far below. Nothing is stopping you from choosing.
Whatever you decide, I will not make you pay for being honest.
On the roof he puts a small notebook beside the coffee. Its pages contain the things he has learned because you chose to tell him.
I know your coffee order. I know which subjects you do not want to discuss. I still don’t know what you will decide tonight.
You notice one blank page labeled THINGS I HAVE YET TO ASK.
I want a life where I never stop being curious about you. But you are not a prize for becoming decent.
The lights of Manhattan make a quiet background to a question no amount of power can answer for you.

then: Dante reserved a table at Mara’s instead of a penthouse gala. He brings no entourage, only a book you recommended.
This is the part of my life I wanted you to see.
Your independent work has become a public part of the waterfront project. Dante thanks you without claiming any share of it.
I am proud of what you built without me.
You and Dante shared a day without any romantic expectation. He respects that possibility even as the final question approaches.
If all we ever are is friends, it still matters to me.

beats: The rooftop wind lifts the edge of Dante's notebook. On the blank page, he has written one question: WHAT WOULD YOU NEED TO FEEL FREE?
I have told you how I feel. What would a yes—or a no—actually mean for you?
You answer in your own words—"Even if I say yes, I keep my work, friends, privacy, and a place that is mine."
Of course. Love cannot mean merging our lives against your will.
He waits, no longer rehearsing an answer.
Whatever happens, I want you to recognize yourself in your future.

beats.hint: What boundary will shape your future?

then: He writes it down only because you ask: Ask, do not track.

opts.t: I am not ready to define terms.
then: He closes the notebook. Then we write nothing tonight.

beats.place: A promise that is not a proposal

beats: Dante meets you at the park bench without a ring, a photographer, or a prearranged speech. In his hand is the receipt for the first public scholarship transfer.
I used to think asking someone to stay required a spectacular reason. That paper is the only thing I brought. It's proof I can follow through on something unglamorous.
You talk about the parts of your life that would exist regardless of him—your work, your friendships, the city you have built around yourself.
If we choose each other, those things stay. If we don't, they still stay.
The confession is almost quiet enough to miss. There is room for an enthusiastic yes, a careful maybe, or a confident no. His face changes, but his respect does not.

choices.t: Choose a committed relationship, on equal terms.
then: 'Then let’s build something neither of us has to escape.'

choices.t: Choose a slow romance, without exclusivity yet.
then: 'Then we keep learning each other. No assumptions. No rush.'

choices.t: Choose friendship or time alone.
then: He nods. 'Thank you for letting me know the truth. I will respect it.'

en.title: The Life After the Headlines

goal.zh: Epilogue and living-world entry.
goal.en: Epilogue and living-world entry.

then: The future you negotiated includes an explicit no-tracking promise. The romantic label does not override it.
Your independent schedule remains yours after the rooftop conversation. Dante does not assume shared calendars.
Because you chose not to define terms, Dante treats ambiguity as a reason to ask, not to presume.

beats: Six months after the rooftop conversation, the old warehouse by Pier Nine has become a community garden and workshop. The scholarship students hold a public exhibition there.
The residents voted on the design themselves. The foundation reports to the community now.
Dante arrives carrying folding chairs, looking deeply offended by the instruction sheet.
I could negotiate the future of a shipping company. Why are there seven screws and only six holes?

then: We chose each other. I keep remembering how carefully you said yes, and I want every ordinary day to honor it.
I know we have not promised exclusivity. I am glad you told me what pace feels right; I will not hurry you.
I heard your decision, and I respect it. This project belongs to you as much as anyone; you never had to love me to belong here.

beats: Later, by the river, Dante gives you a small photograph: the community’s first graduation. On its back he wrote the date and the words WE KEPT OUR PROMISES.
I can’t promise I will never be afraid. I can promise to tell you when I am, and to listen when you are.
Your phone lights up: a new city festival, a message from Elena, and an unread invitation from Dante for an ordinary dinner next Friday.
The rest of our story isn’t a headline. It’s whatever we choose tomorrow.
June introduces the first scholarship graduates. Mara serves lemon cake on paper plates. Elena makes everyone sign the volunteer sheet.
I have survived board votes, federal auditors and my uncle. None of them were as strict as Elena with a clipboard.
Then stop arguing and put your name down. You can help plant trees like everybody else.
The waterfront no longer bears the Moretti crest. It belongs to the people who use it.
Whatever we are to each other now, you helped make this place real. That will always matter.

then: On the Friday after the community celebration, Dante keeps a Friday evening open on his calendar. Not for a board meeting. For you.
You said yes to knowing me. I won't turn that into a lifelong blank check.
You walk through the community kitchen where volunteers are preparing a graduation dinner. No one stands when Dante enters. That is his favorite part.
You two can help chop onions or you can leave. Nobody gets to stand around looking beautiful.
Dante rolls up his sleeves. "I can do onions. I may cry. Please don't make it a headline."
Later he places two keys on the table. One opens his apartment. The other is the spare for the greenhouse.
They're invitations, not expectations. Keep either, neither, or both. We can decide what home means as we go.
The relationship continues: agreed exclusivity, practical boundaries, independent work, optional shared home, Friday dates, no surprise surveillance. Luca's life remains Luca's to decide.
In the weeks after the community celebration, Dante still asks before making plans. Some weeks you say yes. Other weeks you do not. Both answers are real.
I used to send cars. These days I send one message: 'Would you like dinner?' I find I prefer the answer to the performance.
You sit in Mara's restaurant, not quite a couple, not strangers either. He has learned to remember your favorite seat without claiming it.
You know, nothing terrible happens if you two let this take another year.
Dante laughs. "That's the plan. Or it isn't. We get to find out."
He offers you the last lemon tart, then takes it back when you say you want to split it. It feels like a small, ordinary negotiation: the kind both of you can win.
Relationship continues with non-exclusive or undecided terms until explicitly negotiated; no jealousy punishment, no automatic wedding, and autonomous daily lives.

In the weeks after the community celebration, the community center opens its doors without a Moretti name on the wall. You are invited because the residents remember what you did, not because of anyone beside you.
You didn't have to become part of his story to make a difference here.
Dante arrives to deliver folding chairs. He sees you across the courtyard, stops at a comfortable distance, and smiles.
I'm glad you're doing well. No speech, I promise.
You decide whether to share a friendly coffee, exchange a wave, or keep walking toward the exhibition. Nobody follows you.
In time, the news learns to call you by your own name.
Relationship remains platonic or distant as chosen. Independent career and friendships remain playable. Dante does not pursue romance again unless the player explicitly reopens it.

beats: The day after the community celebration, the garden needs watering. Someone has lost the shed key. Life goes on, indifferent to headlines.
The residents elected their oversight committee. June is running for the student seat.
And someone needs to bring lemon cake to the volunteers. I am not doing everything.
Dante looks at you before volunteering your time. "What would you like to do?"
No grand declarations remain. Tomorrow consists of ordinary choices, some together and some apart.
The city remains loud. Your life no longer has to be.

then: Dante wishes you well whatever your relationship status.
June invites you to review a student-led proposal.
You choose a time that suits both people.

beats: At the community opening, a volunteer announces a new exhibit titled THE HERO WHO SAVED THE HARBOR. June immediately asks for the sign to be taken down.
There wasn't one hero. There were tenants, lawyers, teachers, volunteers, and a dozen people who refused to be photographed.
Dante helps carry the old sign out without protesting. The replacement reads THE PEOPLE WHO STAYED.
Elena asks if you would like your name included in the public history archive. You can accept, use an anonymous credit, or keep the record private.
For once, the question of what happens next has no answer written by a billionaire, a crime family, or a reporter. It is only yours—and the people you invited into it.

choices.t: Help plan the next community project.
then: He smiles and asks which ordinary ritual you’d like to make yours.

choices.t: Choose a small personal tradition for the coming month.
then: He offers a standing Friday dinner invitation—one you can decline any time.

choices.t: Take a peaceful break before the next chapter.
then: Dante wishes you well; the community remains yours to visit without him.
